letter.subject: Complaint regarding cookie and tracking activity on arm.com after rejecting cookies
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking activity observed on https://arm.com during an automated, passive audit on 2026-11-08 04:13 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited the site, clicked the cookie banner’s “Reject All” option, browsed a small number of pages, and recorded what cookies were set and what requests were still sent.

The following points were observed or identified during that audit:

1. Google cookies were set before any choice was made on the cookie banner. Five cookies were already set before the banner was answered: VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN and __Secure-YNID. VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, YSC, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN and __Secure-YNID appear to contain unique identifiers.

2. Google still received data after cookies were rejected. After clicking “Reject All”, 10 requests were sent to youtube.com.

3. Adobe cookies were set before any choice was made on the cookie banner. Five cookies were already set before the banner was answered: AMCV_E1D82C1653DA87700A490D4B%40AdobeOrg, demdex, dpm, s_ecid and s_vi. These appear to contain unique identifiers.

4. Adobe still received data after cookies were rejected. After clicking “Reject All”, 55 requests were sent to adobedtm.com.

5. Your privacy policy appears not to name the third parties observed. The policy reviewed names 0 companies, while Adobe and Google were observed. I appreciate the policy may refer to recipients by category only.

6. Our automated review also suggests Adobe tracking may be inconsistent with the cookie policy wording stating: “These cookies allow us to collect anonymous aggregated data on the number of visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our sites or purchases made through our eStore.” Cookies containing what appear to be unique identifiers were observed on Arm’s domain and Adobe’s domains before consent.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking operating without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit shows substantial compliance risk because advertising and analytics technologies were observed before the cookie choice and continued after rejection, although those automated findings are not repeated here. The additional finding is that Adobe identifiers appear inconsistent with the cookie policy's description of Adobe Analytics data as anonymous and aggregated. The privacy statement broadly covers controller identity, purposes, legal bases, sharing, retention, rights and complaints, but does not name the observed providers.
